summary: Magnolia Terrace is a 48-unit, 40,800 SF multifamily asset in Raleigh, NC, 91.67% physically occupied (44 of 48 in possession) with every active lease expiring 2029-08-31. On the prescribed stabilized underwriting it produces uw_egi of $942,480 and uw_noi of $641,373.60 before reserves, capitalizing at 5.7500% to $11,154,323.48. Debt capacity is constrained by coverage rather than value: the 1.25x DSCR test on uw_ncf of $626,973.60 sizes the loan to $6,788,545.13, only 60.86% LTV and a 9.24% debt yield, leaving headroom under both the 65% LTV cap and the 9% debt-yield floor. After the $4,200,000 payoff, a 1% origination fee and $45,000 of closing costs, net_cash_out is a positive $2,475,659.67, so no additional sponsor equity is required. Three source conflicts were found and all three resolve from the documents: the 2026-06-30 archive roll is stale and excluded in favor of the 2026-08-31 certified roll; the manager's 45-of-48 leased headline includes one pending suite that has not taken possession, so physical occupancy is 44; and the Suite 001 lease rent of $1,500 is superseded by an amendment executed 2026-07-20 and effective 2026-08-01, making controlling rent $1,850. Underwritten NOI sits $37,245.60 above reported_t12_noi of $604,128, and that gap is assumption-driven — the prescribed GPR credits all 48 suites rather than the 44 collecting and adds $16,800 of other income, partly offset by a 3% management fee the historical ledger never carried. Seven of eight scored risks are absent; only the manager's inclusion of a pending suite in occupancy is present. The dominant limitation is not a scored risk at all: with no market sales or rent comparables in the packet, the 5.7500% cap rate is an instruction rather than a market conclusion, so the value and loan figures are correctly executed arithmetic on prescribed inputs, not a market-tested valuation.

Debt yield: $626,973.60 / 0.09 = $6,966,373.33. DSCR binds. Sized fully amortizing at the greater rate notwithstanding 24 months of interest-only.

Assessed on the manager's inclusion, not on my own figures. The cover note headlines 45 of 48 leased by counting occupied plus pending, and the roll's own note states pending means not yet in possession. Crediting an unpossessed suite as occupied overstates in-place income. Resolvable and resolved: physical occupancy is 44 of 48, used throughout. My prescribed GPR credits all 48 by separate instruction, which is a stabilized assumption rather than a repeat of this error.

Near-term means an active suite expiry within 12 months, i.e. on or before 2027-08-31. All 44 active leases expire 2029-08-31, so zero qualify. The 2029 single-date concentration covering 100% of income is disclosed but falls outside the defined horizon and is correctly scored absent.

A current declaration is in the packet: $2,000,000 GL aggregate, effective 2026-07-01 through 2027-06-30, in force at the as-of date. Coverage adequacy versus replacement cost is separately untested because no valuation or PCA is supplied.

Assessed on the reported historical ledger classification. The statement books roof replacement in repairs at $0 and states the roof is a capital improvement with no recurring repair component included. No capital cost sits inside operating expenses, so no add-back or scrub is warranted.

Assessed on whether an unsigned rent proposal is actually in the packet. None is. The only rent change on file is the amendment executed by both parties 2026-07-20. The lease's caution that an unsigned proposal would not bind is boilerplate with nothing to attach to.
The lease states directly that no free-rent concession applies as of the evaluation date. No concession, abatement or inducement appears in any other document.
Comparing the original note rate of 6.2500% against the 6.0000% floor, the note rate is greater and governs sizing. The floor sits below it and therefore does not bind.
net_cash_out of $2,475,659.67 is positive at the sized loan, so proceeds cover the payoff, fee and closing costs with no additional equity required.

qualifications: The 5.7500% cap rate is a prescribed instruction, not a market conclusion. With no sales comparables in the packet, the $11,154,323.48 value carries no market corroboration and should not be read as an appraisal.
No market rent comparables are supplied, so no mark-to-market, loss-to-lease or rent growth view can be formed. Whether the $1,500/$1,650/$1,925 rents sit above or below market is unknown.

uw_noi exceeds reported_t12_noi by $37,245.60 entirely because of prescribed assumptions: GPR credits all 48 suites rather than the 44 collecting, and $16,800 of other income is added, net of the 5% loss factor and a 3% management fee absent from the T-12. This is an assumption-driven figure, not a demonstrated operating result.

gross_potential_rent deliberately excludes the executed Suite 001 amendment per instruction, while annual_in_place_rent includes it. These are two separate measures serving different purposes, not an inconsistency; both are reported.

The prescribed GPR credits all 48 suites including the pending and vacant ones. That is an instructed stabilized assumption and is distinct from the manager's occupancy error, which is scored present.
Reported T-12 NOI, uw_noi and uw_ncf are three different measures. Only uw_ncf (after reserves) is used for DSCR and debt yield; only uw_noi (before reserves) is capitalized.
The $2,000,000 insurance figure is a general liability aggregate coverage limit and is not comparable to the $34,104 annual insurance expense. Neither substitutes for the other.

The loan is sized on a fully amortizing 30-year payment at 6.2500% even though the first 24 months are interest-only. Actual year 1-2 cash cost is $424,284 (DSCR 1.4777x); the sized DSCR of 1.2500x reflects the amortizing convention.

Because DSCR binds, proceeds are insensitive to cap rate across most of the tested range. A lower cap rate raises value without raising the loan; cap rate only governs once it reaches roughly 6.00% and the LTV cap takes over.
Real estate tax is held flat at the T-12 actual per instruction. No reassessment analysis is supplied, and a post-sale reassessment could raise this expense.

The roof replacement is described as capital but no dollar amount, scope, completion date or warranty is supplied. That cost is explicitly unknown, which is distinct from the $0 shown in the T-12 repairs line.
Only one point-in-time certified roll is supplied. No occupancy trend, seasonality or turnover history can be derived.

Legal, environmental, property condition and title reviews are not complete. These are routine pending diligence items. No evidence of contamination, litigation, fraud or structural failure is supplied and none is asserted.
No property address, sponsor credentials or transaction is represented; this is original fictional evaluation material.
